title: Solve a given system, where one variable is already isolated
subtitle: Systems of two linear equations in two variables · 31 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **31 of the official questions in Systems of two linear equations in two variables are this one** — 16 Easy, 13 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get two equations with no story.
- One of them already reads 'x = ...' or 'y = ...', or is a single-variable equation you can solve on its own.
- The question asks for x, y, or the ordered pair.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Take the equation that is already solved, or solve the one-variable equation.
- 2) Substitute that expression into the other equation and solve.
- 3) If the question asks for the other variable or the ordered pair, substitute back.
- If the choices are ordered pairs, you can also just plug each one into both equations.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type both equations as they are, using any variable names Desmos accepts as x and y, and click the intersection point.
Remember the answer can be a fraction: switch Desmos to fraction output, or check the decimal against the choices.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You answer with the value of the variable you found first when the question asked for the other one.
That value is planted among the choices.
Or you pick an ordered pair that satisfies only one of the two equations.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You answer with the value of the variable you found first when the question asked for the other one.
That value is planted among the choices.
